newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia bond yields close to lows, shorts resting.
newsitem.headline: Australia bond yields close to lows, shorts resting.

text.p: *Australian bond yields remained close to their initial lows following the strong showing in U.S. Treasuries prior to the weekend, fuelling recent self-induced bullish sentiment.
Australian bond yields remained close to their initial lows following the strong showing in U.S. Treasuries prior to the weekend, fuelling recent self-induced bullish sentiment.
The short end saw some modest profit-taking after its steamy performance on Friday on a weak retail trade report which increased speculation of a further easing in monetary policy.

However, "there is more upside, and it's not clear when it will stop," said David Landsley, Treasury economist at National Australia Bank. "We don't know where the top is and we're just going with it."

The June three-year bond futures contract touched its highest level since February 1994 on Friday at 93.83, while the equivalent cash yield is still some 70 basis points above current official 5.5 percent interest rates.

Meanwhile, the long end was boosted by another advance in the U.S. on foreign buying, and saw the local market outperform the move in early trading to take the Australian/U.S. 10-year bond yield spread to around its lowest in some three years at around the 70 basis point level.
"I think the spread can come in a bit further than it has to date," said Ric Simes, chief economist at Rothschild Australia.
"It (the spread) could come in on either the back of stronger economic data in the States or a continuation of the sentiment we are seeing here," Simes added.
April building approvals released today showed a 3.6 percent increase, much in line with median expectations and compared forecasts ranging from a 7.0 percent rise to a 3.0 percent fall.

The Reserve Bank holds its monthly board meeting on Tuesday, and although a further easing is unlikely so soon after the unexpected rate cut just over a week ago, the market will be taking nothing for granted over the next couple of days.

The local short end gave up some ground to U.S. and Canada after last week's strong outperformance. However, the long end outperformed Canada, which holds its general election today. New Zealand markets were closed for the Queen's Birthday holiday.
